summary: Bryan J. Cuevas is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Emory and the University of Virginia, held a postdoctoral fellowship at Princeton (~2000–2001), and became John F. Priest Professor of Religion at Florida State (~2003).
Bryce Ryan held academic posts at the University of Ceylon in 1950 and at Cornell University around 1951 to 1952.

Bulcsu Siklós worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of London (~1987–1993) under Tadeusz Skorupski and Charles R. Bawden, later holding a post at SOAS University of London (~1992–1998).
Bunkyo Aoki specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. A disciple of Kozui Otani (~1908–1914), he later held a post at the University of Tokyo (~1942–1948).

Bunyiu Nanjio worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology. He studied under F. Max Müller and A. A. Macdonell at Oxford, later becoming Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Tokyo (1885) and President of Otani University (~1914–1923).

Bunzaburo Matsumoto specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. After studying at the University of Tokyo (~1890–1893), he held posts there (~1899–1906) and as a professor at Kyoto University (1906–1929).

Burglind Jungmann works in art history, Sinology, and Japanology. She studied at Seoul National and Heidelberg, and held posts at Heidelberg, Munich, the Los Angeles County Museum of Art, and the University of California, Los Angeles (1999–2017).

Burkhard Quessel is a Tibetologist who studied at the University of Hamburg. He held posts at the University of Hamburg, the University of London, and served as a curator at the British Library (~2001–2017).

Burton Watson was a Sinologist and Japanologist. Educated at Columbia University (~1948–1956), he held academic posts at Kyoto University (~1952–1956), Stanford University (~1962–1963), and Columbia University (~1964–1973).
Bötrül Dongak Tenpé Nyima was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Dzogchen Monastery (1916) under traditional teachers Thubten Nyendrak and Khenpo Genam.

C. D. Sebastian specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. After earning a PhD at Banaras Hindu University (~-2005) and completing postdoctoral studies at Bristol, he became Professor of Indian Philosophy at IIT Bombay (~2009).

C. F. Lee studied at the University of Hong Kong (~1964–1968) and the University of Western Ontario (~1969–1972). He served as Pro-Vice-Chancellor at the University of Hong Kong from 1994 to 2015, working in Buddhist studies.
C. R. Krishnamacharlu was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology who completed studies at Madras Christian College and Pachaiyappa's College.
C. S. Srinivasachariar worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He held professorships at Pachaiyappa's College (~1910–1931) and Annamalai University (~1931–1946).
C. S. Sundaram worked in Indology, holding posts at The Madras Sanskrit College and as Reader in Sanskrit at the University of Madras (1951–1957).

C. W. Huntington specialized in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (~1980–1986) under Luis Oscar Gómez and served as a professor at Hartwick College (~2000–2020).

Calambur Sivaramamurti was an Indologist and historian. He studied under S. Kuppuswami Sastri at Presidency University, Kolkata, and held posts at the Government Museum in Chennai (1935–1946), the Indian Museum (1946), and the National Museum, New Delhi (~1966–1969).

Calvert Watkins was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Harvard University (~1950–1959). He held academic posts at Harvard University (1959–2003) and the University of California, Los Angeles (2003–2013).

Cameron Bailey specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Indiana University under Richard F. Nance, at Florida State University under Bryan J. Cuevas, and earned his doctorate at the University of Oxford under Ulrike Roesler (~2013–2018).

Cameron David Warner is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. After earning a PhD at Harvard University (~2001–2008), he held academic posts at Middlebury College (~2008–2009) and Dickinson College (~2009–2010).
